This applies to every Fell. The whole table is together again here.

> [!reminder] If every Fell fell
> Skip this scene. Go straight to the Defeat ending in [[08 - Dawn on the Sallowrun|Dawn on the Sallowrun]].

> [!reminder] How this scene works
> The fight is over and the night is nearly done. Nib tells the Fell the truth about the shaft and asks them to keep it quiet. There is no roll that decides it. The table chooses, and both answers are fair.
> - **Told.** Everyone learns a Tooth-and-Tool warren let the grey in through its own floor. Nib takes it, and goes down every warren on the river to look for grey roots. Stone warrens may never be built again.
> - **Kept.** Nobody learns it. Nib stays, quiet, and stone keeps its good name. Nobody else learns to look before they dig.
> The answer changes one read-aloud in the ending. Whatever they choose, Nib does not argue.

## If the stone held

This applies if the Fell sealed the shaft.

> [!readaloud] Opening: The hall at dawn
> The great hall is quiet. The floor has a long ridge down the middle where it lifted, and two cracked flagstones, and that's all. Grey light comes in through the river arch. The Shrewish who stayed are asleep on their bundles in heaps, children on top. Nib sits on her upturned bucket by the arch with her head in her paws. Kettle is asleep in the hood of one of your cloaks.

## If the warren is lost

This applies if the shaft was held until the last raft, or never sealed.

> [!readaloud] Opening: The riverbank at dawn
> You come out onto the quay as the light comes up grey over the water. Behind you, through the arch, the floor of the great hall has split down the middle, and soft grey wood fills the crack and keeps rising, slow, filling the room. The rafts are gone, all but the last one, full to the rail, which Dobb is holding at the steps with room for you and no one else. Nib sits on the edge of the quay with her feet over the water. Kettle is asleep on the raft in a coil of rope.

## What Nib says

This applies to every Fell, wherever the scene is set.

> [!dialogue] Nib Sorrelgate
> "There wasn't a drain. You've worked that out, I expect. I dug that shaft. Last spring. I wanted clean water for this place, so we wouldn't have to drink the river, and I went down and down, and I broke into that hollow, and there it was. Grey. All the way through."

> [!dialogue] Nib Sorrelgate
> "I should have walled it with stone right then. I knew it. But stone would've taken me till summer, and I had the new rooms to finish and the Slumpwood folk coming, and I thought clay would hold it a year. I plugged it with clay and I told nobody. Not one person. And tonight it came through my clay and nearly took every one of them."

> [!dialogue] Nib Sorrelgate
> "I'll ask you one thing, and you can say no. Don't tell them it was me. Not because of me. I don't care about me. Because if it comes out that a Tooth-and-Tool warren let the grey in through its own floor, there won't be another stone warren built on Shervinaw, ever. Everybody'll go back to living in the roots and trusting them. And the roots are rotting."

> [!dialogue] Nib Sorrelgate
> *If asked why she didn't tell them before:* "Because I needed you down that shaft, not standing about arguing with me about whose fault it was. And because I'm a coward about it. Both."

> [!dialogue] Nib Sorrelgate
> *If asked whether there are more like it:* "I don't know. That's the truth. If there's one grey root down there nobody mapped, there could be ten. Somebody ought to look. Somebody ought to go down every warren on the river and look."

> [!lorecheck] Spirit: What it would cost her
> Any Fell who looks at Nib and tries to understand her.
>
> - **Fellmark.** *Read:* She means it. She doesn't care what happens to her. She has spent every day since spring waiting for this, and now it's happened, and the only thing she has left to be afraid for is the idea that stone can work. If you tell, she'll stand there and let them say it to her face. *Then:* Their Spirit increases by 1.
> - **Success.** *Read:* She isn't asking for herself.
> - **Failure.** *Read:* You can't read her. She's too tired to show anything.
> - **Fellstrike.** *Read:* You decide she's only protecting herself. *Then:* She isn't. Nothing changes, and the choice is still the table's.

> [!lorecheck] Logic: What it would cost the Tooth-and-Tool
> Any Fell who thinks it through.
>
> - **Fellmark.** *Read:* If the story goes downriver that the stone warren let the grey in, every warren on Shervinaw hears it by summer. The Tooth-and-Tool are already called half mad. Nobody will dig in stone again. And if the story doesn't go, the next Tooth-and-Tool digger doesn't learn to look for grey before they dig. Either way someone pays. *Then:* Their Logic increases by 1.
> - **Success.** *Read:* Telling would end stone warrens. Keeping it means nobody learns to check.
> - **Failure.** *Read:* It seems simple to you. It isn't, and you'll find that out.
> - **Fellstrike.** *Read:* You're sure nobody would believe it was her anyway. *Then:* They would.

**This applies if the Fell talked Furze out of his larder in scene 3.** Partway through, Furze comes up to them, leaning on his stick, and stands listening. He heard enough. Nobody else did. If he stayed in his larder until the floor drove him out, he is somewhere else, counting jars, and does not come.

> [!dialogue] Old Furze
> "Hm. Well. I've filled a larder for forty years and I've put a few bad jars in it in my time. I'll tell you this, though. You don't hide a bad jar. You find out why it went off."

**This applies to every Fell.** Dobb is at the river arch, or holding the last raft at the steps. He heard her too. Read the line that fits what happened to him in scene 4.

> [!dialogue] Dobb
> *If he held his nerve:* "Everybody's got something they don't tell, Nib. Thirty years on the river and nobody knows I can't swim." *He looks at the Fell who brought him back, if anyone did.* "Well. Nearly nobody. Your call, the lot of you. You went down there, not me."

> [!dialogue] Dobb
> *If he froze:* "I stood on that quay tonight and couldn't move, Nib, with twenty of ours going in the water, and these ones had to do it for me. So don't talk to me about getting something wrong." *He looks at the Fell.* "Your call. You went down there, not me."

> [!choice] Tell, or keep it
> - **Tell.** The Fell say what happened, to the Shrewish here and at Quillbark. Write down: the secret was told. Nib stands and lets them hear it, and she doesn't argue.
> - **Keep it.** The Fell say nothing. Write down: the secret was kept. Nib nods and doesn't thank them.
> - **Make her tell it herself.** The Fell won't tell, and they won't keep it for her. Write down: the secret was told. She tells it, standing on her bucket, by noon.
> - **Something else.** The Fell might ask her to go down every warren on the river and look for grey roots, as the price of their silence. Write down: the secret was kept, and she does it. Write down what they asked for.

> [!readaloud] Closing: First light
> Nib picks up her pencils and puts them back behind her ears, one each side, and stands up. Over the river the sky has gone from black to grey. Somewhere behind you, Kettle is waking up and asking whether it is morning yet, and whether anyone saved the plums.

> [!beat] Where everyone is now
> Go to [[08 - Dawn on the Sallowrun|Dawn on the Sallowrun]].
